statement: P0003 as sourced to Grimmett Question 2.2 asks about uniform fixed-n honeycomb SAW from the origin; Duminil-Copin--Smirnov Conjecture 1 asks about critical length-weighted chordal paths between two boundary marks. A proof for the latter does not without transfer prove the former.
assumptions: P0003 is Grimmett Question 2.2 in the existing brain card

quotes: uniformly distributed n-step SAW from the origin
assigning to gamma a weight proportional to x^ell(gamma)

proof_or_counterexample: The sampling rules differ: fixed length and free endpoint versus fixed endpoints and random length. Neither cited source supplies a transfer theorem.
independent_reviewer: w407 (source comparison); w410 pending if promoted as a new mathematical reduction
remaining_gap: Specify fixed-n scaling/topology and prove transfer if using chordal route.

statement: The honeycomb connective constant is sqrt(2+sqrt(2)); Grimmett's displayed sqrt(1+sqrt(2)) conflicts with the proved theorem and is a source typo, not an alternative normalization.
assumptions: Both sources refer to the standard honeycomb SAW connective constant
proof_or_counterexample: Duminil-Copin--Smirnov Theorem 1 proves the latter; compare Grimmett lines 85-87. The two constants are unequal.
remaining_gap: Independent source-row audit before public correction.

statement: For finite positive-weight simple paths on an embedded graph, P(path avoids closed A)=Z(G^A)/Z(G) when G^A deletes vertices and embedded edge segments meeting A.

source.quote: The surviving paths of G^A are exactly the paths of G avoiding A.

proof_or_counterexample: Weight-preserving bijection; conditional law follows when Z(G^A)>0.
remaining_gap: No asymptotic partition-ratio limit or fixed-n transfer.

statement: Under Hausdorff-weak compact-set convergence, convergent avoidance limits for each fixed positive outer buffer determine avoidance of the closed unbuffered obstacle.
assumptions: N_r_m(A) subset A_m subset N_R_m(A), with positive radii tending to zero
each fixed-m q_m exists and q_m converges
proof_or_counterexample: Distance to A is Hausdorff-Lipschitz; Portmanteau gives the strict/non-strict squeeze; both ends tend to P(d>0).
remaining_gap: Fixed-buffer critical SAW ratios are unproved.

statement: Uniform convergence of simple curves need not preserve avoidance of a closed boundary-attached obstacle.

source.quote: Each trace avoids A; its deterministic avoidance probability is 1.

proof_or_counterexample: For central x, gamma_n has y>0; its uniform limit lies at y=0 and meets A.
remaining_gap: Only refutes raw event transfer, not SAW scaling.

statement: For connected finite honeycomb internal graph with zero boundary-halfedge data, the local vertex-relation kernel has complex dimension |E_int|-|V|+1; an interior hexagon gives bounded modes with adjacent unit jumps at distance sqrt(3)delta/2.
assumptions: regular hexagonal face of side delta
proof_or_counterexample: Reweighted vertex equations are B X=0, incidence rank |V|-1. Face circulation X_e=delta/2 gives F(m_e)=delta/d_e, supnorm 1 and adjacent jump 1.
remaining_gap: The mode need not be an actual SAW path-sum; extra SAW estimate may suppress it.

verdict: FIX for conditional chordal claim; DROP as direct P0003 reduction
statement: Under T/B/C the route may identify the critical length-weighted chordal trace as SLE(8/3), subject to full LSW hull coverage and trace-to-curve measurability; it does not address fixed-n origin SAW without transfer.

source.quote: Assume these unproved inputs: T... B... C...

proof_or_counterexample: LSW needs smooth-hull avoidance formula on its sample space. T and B remain unproved; Grimmett Question 2.2 samples a different ensemble.
remaining_gap: LSW class coverage, trace-to-curve step, T, B and fixed-n transfer.
